title: Her mother's death (1877)
hook: her earliest sharp memory: being lifted to kiss her mother's forehead, and a coffin that seemed very big
tomorrow: her sister became her second mother. then she overheard something.

segments.voice: A week of turning pages: a bow let slack, a pull that isn't a yes, a bird in a net, a clock cleaned, a notebook begun, a garden of flowers. Yesterday's line: every flower.

Earliest memories are strange. Not the big picture, just small, sharp pieces: a doorway, a smell, the height of a table. Thérèse kept one she never lost. Her father lifts her up to kiss her mother's forehead one last time. She doesn't cry. She doesn't say a word. Years later, writing as a young nun, she remembers that the coffin seemed very big, and she had to look up at it.
screen: `SMALL, SHARP PIECES.` → `LIFTED UP FOR ONE LAST KISS.` → `THE COFFIN SEEMED VERY BIG.`

segments.voice: First, the sunny start. Thérèse remembers her earliest years as bright: a loving home, a lively, cheerful little girl, and, she admits, a stubborn one. Then the loss. Her mother died after an illness, and Thérèse writes that she was four and a half. Then the change, the line the rest of the book leans on. After her mother's death, she says, her happy temperament changed completely. The lively child became timid and oversensitive. A look could make her cry. Then the choice. After the funeral, Céline threw herself into Marie's arms: you'll be my mother. Thérèse, not wanting to be left out, ran to Pauline: then Pauline will be my mother. Notice how she tells it. She doesn't hurry past the grief or turn it straight into a lesson. She lets the loss be real, lets it change her, and says so in plain words.
screen: `A SUNNY, STUBBORN START.` · `FOUR AND A HALF.` · `HER TEMPERAMENT CHANGED.` · `PAULINE WILL BE MY MOTHER.` · then, large: `FOUR YEARS OLD.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and hold in mind a child somewhere who has lost a mother, or the child you once were, if that's your story. If you pray, you can ask Mary, whom Catholics honor as a mother, to keep them close.
Her mother's death. The loss at four and a half that, in Thérèse's own account, changed her completely.
Carry this: four years old, because grief that comes so young still counts. Take care today.
